correctness.rationale: The corrected result is /workspace/repairs/2/RESULT.md. The original general theorem follows under its hypotheses, but the displayed second current and four numerical examples have f''(0)=0, contrary to a literal all-domain f''<0 reading. The repair specifies strict curvature on the open gas density interval, retaining a nondegenerate interior peak and f'(0)>0; the verification script and scientific notes remain applicable, unaltered. Re-derived under the corrected assumptions: summing and subtracting gives S'=-rρ and R'=−(r+α)σ. With c=√(r/(r+α)), D=S−cR satisfies D'=(Λ/v)D; its absolute value cannot decrease in the positive-speed tail, so decay sets it to zero and flux continuity and ODE uniqueness preserve zero in the core. Hence R'=-Λρ and R is Λ times remaining rightward tail mass, with R(0+)=MΛ/2. Reflection yields jumps of ±rM/2 in the two directional transport fluxes, exactly cancelling the two resetting sources. The increasing-branch inverse exists out to infinity since f'(0)>0, and monotonicity prevents a decreasing-current-side gas tail. Peak equality gives a continuous cusp but a well-defined flux and weak gas solution; Taylor expansion at the peak gives the claimed origin-density fold. Interface flux J sets tail mass J/Λ and fixes the lower gas root; the linear dense current yields exponential density and a core iff MΛ/2>J. The derivative of (log t)/t changes only at e for t>1, so the strict coexistence comparisons, including upper equality, and the mass fraction follow. The two examples have maxima 2 and 16/(3√3) by differentiation, on opposite sides of e for common J=1; both now satisfy the stated curvature condition. No dynamical conclusion is claimed.

value.rationale: At fixed dense flux and kinetic controls, varying the gas shape leaves the optimal droplet size and mass partition unchanged but can switch whether a competing stationary gas state exists at that optimum. The explicit admissible pair isolates that effect, giving a sharp criterion usable to separate geometric optimization from branch availability. The claimed value does not rest on an isolated derivative calculation, a new name for the flux integral, or a claim of experimental hysteresis.
